one_line_reason: Multiple independent OTC-laxative systematic reviews give senna 'good (grade A)' evidence for chronic constipation, the classic outcome it is marketed for, though as qualitative synthesis rather than a single pooled effect size.

selected.population: adults with chronic constipation (updated systematic review of 41 RCTs ≥4 weeks)
selected.intervention: oral senna (stimulant laxative) vs other OTC constipation treatments or placebo
selected.why_selected: Systematic review grading senna as 'good evidence (grade A recommendation)' for chronic constipation, on par with polyethylene glycol

selected.population: adults with chronic constipation (synopsis of an updated systematic review, 41 RCTs)
selected.intervention: oral senna vs other OTC constipation treatments
selected.why_selected: A companion/updated publication reaching the same grade-A conclusion for senna as first-line therapy; included as corroborating evidence though likely drawing on an overlapping trial base with 33767108

selected.population: long-term care (nursing home) patients (7 RCTs, 444 patients)
selected.intervention: oral senna (with or without fibre) vs lactulose, sodium picosulphate, docusate, PEG, or Chinese herbal medicine
selected.why_selected: Independent systematic review in an older, institutionalized population finding senna superior to or as effective as other studied laxatives

selected.intervention: senna-based bowel preparation regimen vs other bowel-prep regimens
selected.why_selected: A different, well-quantified use case (pre-colonoscopy bowel prep) where senna showed no significant advantage in bowel cleanliness versus comparators, despite better patient tolerance/compliance -- useful counterpoint showing senna's efficacy is outcome-specific

blockers: 33767108 and 35943487 appear to be closely related/updated publications from the same review program and likely share much of the same underlying trial evidence, so they should not be double-counted as independent confirmations
None of the selected reviews states a specific senna dose or effect size (e.g., relative risk) for the constipation-relief claim; the grading is qualitative (grade A/B/C)
35758925's bowel-prep use case (single large-volume dose before colonoscopy) is a different exposure pattern from the low-dose chronic-use constipation claim most catalog senna products market

excluded_pmids.reason: Meta-analysis pools senna (2 RCTs) together with kiwifruit, magnesium oxide, Ziziphus jujuba, and Malva sylvestris; no senna-specific pooled effect size is given in the retrieved abstract text
Cochrane review of interventions for preventing postpartum constipation broadly; senna is not isolated with specific results in the retrieved abstract
Systematic review of cost-effectiveness of constipation treatments; an economic analysis, not an efficacy trial
Cochrane review of osmotic and stimulant laxatives for childhood constipation; senna-specific results are not isolated in the retrieved abstract
Cochrane review of laxatives in palliative care; the authors explicitly state they drew no conclusions on individual laxative effectiveness due to limited evaluations
One trial within this IBD colon-cleansing review compared senna to castor oil and found no difference; small, clinical (IBD) population and not senna's marketed constipation-relief use case
Review of adjuncts to colonic cleansing before colonoscopy; senna is discussed as one of several adjuncts without isolated efficacy data in the retrieved abstract

Tropical forestry study of tree-legume fertilization; 'Senna reticulata' here is an unrelated tree species sharing the genus name, not the medicinal senna (Cassia/Senna alexandrina) used in laxative supplements
